name: FLU-A H3N2
interpretation:
TEST INFORMATION
Influenza Virus: Influenza virus (family orthomyxoviridae) is single stranded RNA genome that is present in 8 separate segments of ribonucleoprotein. This segmentation of the genome is rare among viruses and it may contribute to a rapid development of new influenza strains through the interchange of gene segments between viruses infecting the normal cell. There are 3 types of influenza viruses: A, B & C. A and B viruses are most common among three. Especially Type A virus is known to be common for infecting not only human, but also birds and various types of mammals. Among the influenza viruses that invade humans, H1N1 and H3N2 are becoming problem for infecting children and elders. Type B and C are limited to affecting human only. The symptoms for having influenza is nasal discharge, nasal congestion, chill and muscle pain, which are severe than regular cold. Characteristically, influenza symptom include high fever and develop complications due to bacterial infections.


Seasonal Influenza: Seasonal influenza is an acute viral infection caused by an influenza virus. Type A influenza viruses are further divided into subtypes according to the combinations of viral surface proteins. Among many subtypes of influenza A virus, H1N1 and H3N2 subtypes are the recent ones circulating among humans. Influenza viruses circulate in every part of the world. Type C influenza virus cases occur much less frequently than type A and B. That is why only influenza A and B viruses are included in seasonal influenza vaccines. Influenza epidemics occur yearly during autumn and winter in the temperate regions. Illnesses result in hospitalizations and deaths mainly among high-risk groups (infant, elderly or chronically ill). Worldwide, these annual epidemics result in about three to five million cases of severe illness, and about 250,000 to 500,000 deaths. Most deaths associated with influenza in industrialized countries occur among people age 65 or older.
